fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Tom Barnett is a master of the flow state, and teaches people to build their optimized self through movement, breathing, nutrition, thinking, feeling, and rest. As simple as these things may be, most of us are doing them wrong in some way or another. In this episode we talk about combining these elements to upgrade our bodies and the consciousness driving them, we discuss male monthly energy cycles and how the moon relates, strategies for balancing work outs with "working in" and give examples of how to do that, we riff on sexual health and the pitfalls of modern times, and a lot more.

fields.Plus Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Image Is Never the Goal", "body": "Chance argues that a self-image you must reach before you feel okay is a moving goalpost, because an image lives in the imagination and the real issue is not accepting yourself as you are, and he reminds listeners that someone always looks up to them, so running yourself down poisons the whole field around you. Tom adds that every energy on the planet has its complementary opposite, so whatever quirk you dislike is exactly what someone else is looking for, and drawing on his work as a photographer with Instagram personalities he says many people selling the image of a great life are living worse lives than their audience."}, {"title": "Risk Is the Price of Being Alive", "body": "Tom describes the stories people hold onto, like being unlovable or never able to play guitar on stage, as protective mechanisms that remove all risk and therefore all fulfillment, since you have to risk not being loved in order to be loved. Looking back, he says, nearly every proud memory involved putting yourself out there and being okay with sucking at something. He treats excuses about time, energy and money as a program you can rewrite at any moment, while Chance counters that nature offers no safety net at all, and that we fear public speaking more than the fast food that is genuinely risky for us."}, {"title": "Offer, Acceptance and the Melbourne Model", "body": "Chance notes that danger is a legal idea tied to jurisdiction and asks what Australia's lockdowns reveal. Tom, speaking from his own perspective, calls Melbourne a stage for a model meant to spread, argues that people speak a future of lockdowns and restrictions into reality whether they want it or fear it, and claims Australian government bodies operate as foreign corporations while overseas buyers play a long game for the country's minerals. He still says he has a ton of faith in the human spirit, likening it to a thousand kids who, pushed far enough, overwhelm anyone, and insists that simply declining the offer is the way through."}, {"title": "Quitting the Monopoly Game", "body": "Chance compares the economic system to a Monopoly game where grandma owns nearly every property, and proposes an organized quitting rather than a revolution, such as friends planning a biodynamic farm together over five years. Tom warns that freed zoo animals often return to their cages for food and security, so any new community needs to offer people safety and self-worth. He says he learned just enough commerce to know who asks and who answers the questions, describes money as fish flakes created from debt that push up the price of houses, food and rent, and argues that nobody can truly own the land they caretake."}, {"title": "Truth, Honesty and Going With the Flow", "body": "Chance raises germ theory versus terrain theory as a matter of personal responsibility, and Tom observes that truth is hard to sell while fear is easy to hype, adding that more integrity often means less money. Chance answers that truth needs no proof because it is self-evident, and that the modern economy and society are the real alternatives. Tom says honesty with yourself means you cannot be wrong, that dropping the need to be right removes a major source of stress, and that walking with life after running out of money has always opened a door, which Chance frames as the flow state, synchronicity in motion."}]
